entry.evidence: The large number of geoid models stored in the ISG repository offers the possibility of assessing them through relative comparisons.

sequences.source_document: Published paper (XML text with PDF for figures)

steps.action: The authors inventory the ISG repository, which their own group maintains, and count the Asia–Pacific geoid models it holds by access class and model type.
steps.quote: As for the Asia–Pacific region, there are 58 geoid models, among which 47 are classified as public, 2 as on-demand, and 9 as private.

steps.action: The authors set the aim of comparing the archived Asia–Pacific geoid models to give a picture of geoid knowledge in the region.
steps.quote: This work aims at performing some analyses and comparisons on the geoid models that cover the Asia–Pacific area

steps.action: The authors design three comparisons: a time series of editions for one country, local against regional models, and local against global models.
steps.quote: In this study, three kinds of analyses are provided

steps.action: The authors fix the residual procedure: mask to the overlap, interpolate onto the coarser grid, synthesize global models on the local grid, and remove a best-fitting plane to absorb frame and datum offsets.
steps.quote: the grid of the model with the lower resolution is taken as reference

steps.action: The authors compare summary statistics of the PGM2014, PGM2016 and PGM2018 Philippine series and match an 80 cm bias to the tide-gauge shift reported by the original authors.
steps.quote: Statistics reveal a bias of about 80 cm between the first PGM2014 and the subsequent PGM models

steps.action: The authors compute plane-reduced residuals between successive PGM editions and map them, finding sub-centimetre differences for 2014 to 2016 and about 3 cm STD with trench-related structure for 2016 to 2018.
steps.quote: PGM2014 and PGM2016 show a very good agreement, with a sub-centimetric standard deviation

steps.action: The authors attribute the high-frequency PGM2018 differences to new satellite gravity, altimetry and densified land gravity data, and do not test this explanation.
steps.quote: This is probably thanks to new satellite gravity and altimetry data and densified land gravity data

steps.action: The authors apply the same series comparison to the Australian, Japanese, Hawaiian and New Zealand series (Table 3) and read a decreasing residual STD with each update.
steps.quote: the standard deviation of the residuals decreases gradually with updating the model

steps.action: The authors explain the near-zero GEOID99–USGG03 residuals, which break the monotone pattern, as two identical models that differ only in reference frame.
steps.quote: these two gravimetric models are the same for the Hawaiian Islands but for the reference frame

steps.action: The authors compare the 1999 SEA regional model with downsampled PGM2018 and Brunei local geoids and find residuals (STD 1.19 m and 0.5 m) far above the declared local accuracies.
steps.quote: These residuals are quite higher if compared to the expected accuracy (declared by authors) of PGM2018 and Brunei geoids

steps.action: The authors check the same local models against EGM2008 as a reference and find much better agreement, which supports the judgement that SEA is outdated.
steps.quote: the agreement with EGM2008 is considerably higher for both PGM2018 (STD 0.184 m) and Brunei (STD 0.103 m)

steps.action: The authors evaluate the gravimetric and hybrid TWGEOID2018 against EGM2008 and EIGEN6C4, synthesized with ICGEM tools on the same grid, and compare means, STDs and residuals.
steps.quote: slightly better matching between TWGEOID2018 and EGM2008 is revealed, accordingly to the input data used for its computation

steps.action: The authors map the Taiwan residuals and locate the main differences on the Chinese mainland, the Yaeyama Islands and off Quanzhou, attributing them to data gaps.
steps.quote: the local Taiwanese geoid model seems to provide more detailed information than the global models

steps.action: The authors apply the local-global comparison to every Asia–Pacific model in the repository (Table 8) and find that agreement varies by region.
steps.quote: the agreement between local and global geoid models is different depending on the considered area

steps.action: The authors compare the threefold better EGM2008 fit for Xinjiang and Tibet with Shen and Han (2013), who report that the model was built on EGM2008.
steps.quote: This result matches what can be found in Shen and Han (22)

steps.action: The authors take from Kostelecky et al. (2015) the expectation that GOCE data improve EIGEN6C4 in remote areas, and suggest it may be the better reference despite worse statistics.
steps.quote: EIGEN6C4 might be a better reference for local model assessment

steps.action: The authors notice anomalous minimum and maximum residuals for the Russian RGG2003 quasi-geoid, with a normal STD, and assume outliers in the dataset.
steps.quote: This leads assuming the presence of outliers in the dataset.

steps.action: The authors detect outliers by inspecting the residual histogram, correct 4 of 651,689 points, and recompute: the range shrinks while the STD barely changes (RGG2003 g-clean).
steps.quote: correcting just 4 points out of 651,689, the range of residuals significantly decreases

steps.action: The authors tabulate the mean values of local and global models on the same grids and read them as evidence of differing height datums.
steps.quote: These values clearly show how the adopted height datums are different

steps.action: The authors keep three summary findings: successive editions converge, the SEA regional model is outdated, and local models agree with global ones to a few to tens of centimetres in STD.
steps.quote: in all geoid series, there is a time trend with smaller and smaller corrections

tree.answer: Successive editions across several countries repeat the series comparison
Trend repeats across series once the Hawaii exception is explained; outlier cleaning leaves the STD unchanged

end.claim: Across the Asia–Pacific geoid series stored at ISG, residuals between successive editions shrink over time, indicating progressive refinement toward an optimal solution; this headline is accompanied by the findings that local models agree with EGM2008 and EIGEN6C4 to a few to tens of centimetres and that the 1999 SEA regional model is outdated.

decisive_move.sentence: Extending the edition-to-edition residual comparison from the Philippine example to all multi-edition series in the repository (Table 3) is what turns one case into the claimed time trend across all series.

gates.evidence: The data are pre-existing archived models; no hypothesis directed their acquisition (§1.1 ¶1). The decreasing-residual trend could have failed across the Table 3 series. It is not monotone for Hawaii (GEOID99–USGG03 0.001 m, then USGG03–USGG09 0.116 m), and the authors explain that exception rather than count it against the trend (§2.1 ¶6). Nothing is stated as fixed in advance: no thresholds or expected values are given before the comparisons.

imports.item: Outlier detection by histogram inspection of residuals, with removal and interpolation
Least-squares best-fitting plane removed from residuals to absorb frame and datum offsets

limits: No review file or earlier version was supplied, so no review sequence is coded. All checks are relative comparisons among models: there is no independent GNSS/levelling or gravity validation, no uncertainty on the residual statistics, and declared accuracies are taken from the original authors. The headline 'all geoid series' trend rests on Table 3, which covers only series with at least three models; the Philippine PGM series appears only in Table 2. The Hawaii exception is explained by an auxiliary fact (identical models, different frame) rather than treated as a counterexample (inference). Explanations of residual patterns (new satellite and altimetry data for PGM2018, data gaps for Taiwan) are hedged ('probably') and untested. Sub-claims and their statuses: SEA regional model outdated relative to recent global models, best_explanation; local and global agreement of a few to tens of centimetres in STD, estimate_with_resolution, but without stated uncertainty; height datums differ (Table 9), regularity_in_range, descriptive. The reason for preferring EIGEN6C4 in remote areas is cited from Kostelecky et al., not tested here. Table 8 has an apparent typo (Vietnam EGM2008 min '−1322'). Composition is none_fits: the work is a descriptive inter-comparison of archived models, with no stated rivals, no crucial test, and no found or set conditions in the sense of the listed compositions. Its repetitions are successive model editions, not repetitions by nature.

disagreements.support: Residuals against PGM2018 (STD 1.19 m) and Brunei (STD 0.5 m) far exceed the local models' declared accuracies, and EGM2008 agrees much better with both local models.
disagreements.quote: These residuals are quite higher if compared to the expected accuracy (declared by authors) of PGM2018 and Brunei geoids

disagreements.support: The gravimetric model's mean matches EIGEN6C4 although it was reportedly computed with EGM2008, which the authors call contradictory.
disagreements.quote: the statistics of Table 6 are quite contradictory

disagreements.target: Russian quasi-geoid model RGG2003 (Medvedev and Nepoklonov 2003)
disagreements.support: Residual extremes of tens of metres with a normal STD point to outliers; correcting 4 points shrinks the range while leaving the STD almost unchanged.

alternatives_considered.alternatives: Interpolation onto a finer grid (implied by the reason)
alternatives_considered.reason: Conservative: avoids adding gross artefacts from the interpolation method and allows small inconsistencies to be neglected
